focus: Continuity save/resume writer routing: where decisions, summary and handover actually go, plus a live run of generate-context.js against a scratch packet

graphEvents.label: Does continuity save and resume route content where the v4.0.0.13-v4.0.1.0 notes say it does?
CROSS_ANCHOR_CONTAMINATION never receives a routing payload and always passes
save-workflow.md Canonical Save Router describes a router with no code
Eight documented route categories versus five coded ones can never agree
Project-root resolution silently falls back to the runtime repository
A guard refusal is printed as Unexpected Error with a misleading collision class
--planner-mode hybrid is accepted and never branched on
handover_state to handover.md is asserted by five doc rows and implemented by none

label: CROSS_ANCHOR_CONTAMINATION is a registered validate rule that can never run: validateCrossAnchorContamination returns the skip result when no plan is supplied (spec-doc-structure.ts:1289 'No routing payload supplied; contamination check skipped'), and grep -rn contaminationPlan over runtime/cli returns no non-test producer, so the only plan in the repository is the one a unit test hand-builds at tests/spec-doc-structure.vitest.ts:646. The writer cannot supply one either: generate-context.ts mentions routeAs once, in help text, as accepted for compatibility.

release: introduced in commit 5399875c9e (docs 026), unfixed at v4.0.2.0
label: save-workflow.md section Canonical Save Router (lines 413-437) documents a live three-tier router: eight categories, Tier 2 prototype similarity, Tier 3 via LLM_REFORMULATION_ENDPOINT (line 432), a drop refusal writing scratch/pending-route-<hash>.json (line 426), and routeAs forcing a category (line 435). None has code: grep for LLM_REFORMULATION_ENDPOINT or pending-route across .skilled returns only those save-workflow.md lines, and routeAs occurs once in the 1307-line writer inside its help string (generate-context.ts:168). The section is what /speckit:save sends a model to for routing decisions, so a model that uses routeAs believes a category was honoured and the writer writes nothing to it.

The route vocabulary drifted on the doc side only. ROUTE_CATEGORY_ALIASES holds dynamic five categories plus drop (spec-doc-structure.ts:175-184) and inferCategory returns only those same values (spec-doc-structure.ts:1272-1283), while the doc names eight including narrative_delivery, decision, handover_state and research_finding (save-workflow.md:419-426). A declared value for any of those four falls through unchanged at the alias lookup (spec-doc-structure.ts:1297) and must then mismatch the inferred value, emitting SPECDOC_CONTAM_001/002 as a warning by construction (spec-doc-structure.ts:1316).

resolveProjectRoot silently falls back to the runtime repository when the caller's git top-level does not 'use spec-kit', writing one stderr note and continuing (core/config.ts:139-147). The writer help promises the opposite default: --project-root defaults to the git top-level of the working directory and must sit inside it (generate-context.ts:99). Probe run this iteration from a git init scratch repo holding specs/001-probe printed '[spec-kit] /private/tmp/iter8-probe is not inside a repository that uses spec-kit; using the runtime repository /Users/.../Skilled as the project root' and then targeted this checkout, blocked only by the write guard (core/spec-root-write-guard.ts:29). Verify: rerun the probe without --project-root and inspect stderr line 1.

A legitimate write-guard refusal is classified as unexpected: the writer's isExpected pattern list (generate-context.ts:1266) does not include the guard's 'Spec packet write blocked' text, so the probe printed the refusal three times as 'Unexpected Error:', 'Error:' and a stack trace. The message itself reports 'collision class is divergent-duplicate (no readable packet roots)' (core/spec-root-write-guard.ts:29) for what was a packet absent from a root that exists.

--planner-mode hybrid is accepted and has no behaviour. It is in the union (generate-context.ts:45), validated as one of three legal values (generate-context.ts:1003), and never compared: every consumer branches on plannerMode !== 'full-auto' (core/workflow.ts:577, :702, :2208) or === 'full-auto' (:1982, :1987). The help already concedes it: 'hybrid behaves like plan-only' (generate-context.ts:97). Removing it breaks nothing but two union members, one validation entry and two help lines; keeping it lets a caller pass a name that implies partial writes and receive a plan-only response with no notice.

release: handover claims entered at v4.0.0.13, unchanged through v4.0.2.0
label: handover_state routing to handover.md is asserted by five doc rows (save-workflow.md:340 and :422, SKILL.md:74, templates/template-guide.md:566, templates/level-specifications.md:732) and implemented by none: generate-context.ts contains zero occurrences of 'handover' (grep -c returns 0), so /speckit:save cannot create or refresh handover.md. Thirty-three packets nonetheless carry one (12 at three levels, 21 at four), so the artifact is real and its maintenance route is not. This is the writer-side half of the iteration-6 finding about /speckit:handoff discoverability.

A --full-auto save with a thin payload is refused, not persisted: the run exits 1 with INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT (title too generic, primary evidence 0, semantic substance 36 chars) and writes no file in the target packet. The JSON-primary path therefore cannot silently persist an empty continuity block.

direction: Reading output line counts grep of the writer's dist bundle as evidence of a second implementation
reason: dist/continuity/generate-context.js carries the same single routeAs occurrence as the .ts source, so it is a compiled copy, not a divergent implementation. Symlink and duplicate checks were made before treating either as separate evidence.
